edges.description: Develops CNS demyelination and giant axonopathy, rescued by AAV gene delivery.
edges.limitations: Mouse lifespan and myelin lipid composition differ from human, and patients have not been shown to have giant axons.

edges.description: Contacts are measured directly in liver.
edges.limitations: Contact loss was quantified in liver, not in brain or retina where disease occurs.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying treatment exists for patients; care is supportive. In the Acbd5 Gly357* mouse, adeno-associated virus delivery of Acbd5 improved gait, reduced giant axonopathy, and improved myelination and astrocyte reactivity. This has not been tested in humans.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with giant axonopathy in Acbd5-deficient mice halted by adeno-associated virus gene therapy.
evidence.snippet: We also show that an adeno-associated virus-mediated gene delivery ameliorated the gait phenotypes and the giant axonopathy, also improving myelination and astrocyte reactivity.

evidence.reference_title: ACBD5 / acyl-CoA binding domain containing protein 5 deficiency (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: The mechanism for disease is expected to be loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: Autozygome-guided exome sequencing in retinal dystrophy patients reveals pathogenetic mutations and novel candidate disease genes.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, our study revealed six novel candidate disease genes (C21orf2, EMC1, KIAA1549, GPR125, ACBD5, and DTHD1), two of which (ACBD5 and DTHD1) were observed in the context of syndromic forms of RD that are described for the first time.

evidence.reference_title: ACBD5 deficiency causes a defect in peroxisomal very long-chain fatty acid metabolism.
evidence.snippet: We identified a homozygous deleterious indel mutation in ACBD5, leading to complete loss of ACBD5 protein in the patient.

nodes.description: Biallelic loss-of-function variants remove ACBD5 from the peroxisomal membrane. The protein does two separable things there, so its loss starts two branches: loss of very-long-chain acyl-CoA capture, and loss of the peroxisome-ER tether.

evidence.reference_title: ACBD5 deficiency causes a defect in peroxisomal very long-chain fatty acid metabolism.
evidence.snippet: We identified a homozygous deleterious indel mutation in ACBD5, leading to complete loss of ACBD5 protein in the patient.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of a Retinal Dystrophy Protein, Acyl-CoA Binding Domain-containing 5 (ACBD5), Impairs Peroxisomal β-Oxidation of Very-long-chain Fatty Acids.
evidence.snippet: We herein report that ACBD5 is a peroxisomal tail-anchored membrane protein exposing its ACBD to the cytosol.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of a Retinal Dystrophy Protein, Acyl-CoA Binding Domain-containing 5 (ACBD5), Impairs Peroxisomal β-Oxidation of Very-long-chain Fatty Acids.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, ACBD5 preferentially binds very-long-chain fatty acyl-CoAs (VLC-CoAs).

nodes.description: Loss-of-function mouse showing raised VLCFA, progressive cerebellar pathology, sharply reduced peroxisome-ER contacts in liver, and retinal degeneration with VLC-PUFA accumulation in the plexiform layers.
Truncating mouse allele that reproduces reduced survival, impaired locomotion, photoreceptor loss, demyelination, Purkinje cell loss and giant axonopathy.
Untethered peroxisomes move more, fail to expand their membranes normally, and in mouse liver become more numerous. Peroxisomal calcium uptake, which depends on the contact, is also reduced.

evidence.reference_title: ACBD5 and VAPB mediate membrane associations between peroxisomes and the ER.
evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that loss of PO-ER association perturbs PO membrane expansion and increases PO movement

evidence.reference_title: Peroxisome calcium uptake is dependent on ER-peroxisome membrane contact.
evidence.snippet: we find that the ACBD5-dependent membrane contact site between peroxisomes and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is necessary for efficient peroxisomal Ca2+ uptake

evidence.reference_title: Retinal Dystrophy and Leukodystrophy Caused by ACBD5 Deficiency in Five Omani Patients: A Case Series.
evidence.snippet: First presentation was in infancy with nystagmus and photophobia and progressed to legal blindness by 10 years of age.

nodes.description: Progressive leukodystrophy in patients corresponds, in the Acbd5 Gly357* mouse, to demyelination with giant axonal swellings throughout the central nervous system and reactive astrocytes. AAV delivery of Acbd5 reduced the axonopathy and improved myelination.

evidence.reference_title: Ataxia with giant axonopathy in Acbd5-deficient mice halted by adeno-associated virus gene therapy.
evidence.snippet: Gly357* mutant mice recapitulated key features of the human disorder, including reduced survival, impaired locomotion and reflexes, loss of photoreceptors, and demyelination.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal Dystrophy and Leukodystrophy Caused by ACBD5 Deficiency in Five Omani Patients: A Case Series.
evidence.snippet: Brain MRI revealed diffuse T2 signal abnormality in deep white matter, with involvement of corticospinal tracts.

nodes.description: The ataxia of the Acbd5 Gly357* mouse involves loss of cerebellar Purkinje cells, and ACBD5-deficient mice develop progressive cerebellar pathology.

evidence.snippet: The ataxic presentation of Gly357* mice involved the loss of cerebellar Purkinje cells and a giant axonopathy throughout the CNS.

evidence.snippet: Motor neuroregression with variable ages of onset and signs of progressive cerebellar ataxia were seen in all patients, whereas cognitive decline was observed in some.

evidence.reference_title: First reported adult patient with retinal dystrophy and leukodystrophy caused by a novel ACBD5 variant: A case report and review of literature.
evidence.snippet: Here, we present a 36-year-old female with retinal dystrophy, leukodystrophy, and psychomotor regression due to a novel homozygous variant in ACBD5.

evidence.reference_title: A Novel Homozygous ACBD5 Variant in an Emerging Peroxisomal Disorder Presenting with Retinal Dystrophy and a Review of the Literature.
evidence.snippet: A 6-year-old male patient was admitted with complaints of neuromotor regression and visual disturbances.

nodes.description: Ether lipid (plasmalogen) synthesis starts in the peroxisome and is finished in the ER, so it depends on the two organelles being in contact. Loss of the ACBD5 tether lowers plasmalogen synthesis in cultured cells and shifts ether lipid intermediates in ACBD5-deficient mouse liver. Patient fibroblasts with VLCFA oxidation defects, ACBD5-deficient lines among them, have reduced ether phospholipids. Whether this deficit contributes to the leukodystrophy has not been tested (see discussions).

evidence.reference_title: Cerebellar and hepatic alterations in ACBD5-deficient mice are associated with unexpected, distinct alterations in cellular lipid homeostasis.
evidence.snippet: By contrast, ether lipid formation was perturbed in liver towards an accumulation of alkyldiacylglycerols.

evidence.reference_title: Functional characterisation of peroxisomal β-oxidation disorders in fibroblasts using lipidomics.
evidence.snippet: Remarkably, we found that ether phospholipids, including plasmalogens, were decreased.

nodes.description: Without ACBD5 to capture very-long-chain acyl-CoAs (such as C26:0-CoA) on the cytosolic face of the peroxisome, their transfer into the peroxisome and beta-oxidation slow. The defect is moderate, which fits the mildly raised or normal plasma VLCFA seen in patients. The tethering function is not strictly required for this step in cultured cells, so this branch is modelled separately from the contact-site branch.

evidence.snippet: We show that the tethering function of ACBD5 is not absolutely required for efficient peroxisomal β-oxidation of VLCFAs.

nodes.description: ACBD5 binds ER VAPA and VAPB through its FFAT-like motif and is the main tether holding peroxisomes against the ER. Without it, peroxisome-ER contacts are sharply reduced, and the lipid exchange, calcium uptake and positioning that depend on the contact fail.

evidence.reference_title: VAPs and ACBD5 tether peroxisomes to the ER for peroxisome maintenance and lipid homeostasis.
evidence.snippet: Depletion of either ACBD5 or VAP expression results in increased peroxisome mobility, suggesting that VAP-ACBD5 complex acts as the primary ER-peroxisome tether.

evidence.reference_title: Cerebellar and hepatic alterations in ACBD5-deficient mice are associated with unexpected, distinct alterations in cellular lipid homeostasis.

nodes.description: In ACBD5-deficient mice, photoreceptor, bipolar, ganglion and pigment epithelial cells degenerate moderately, photoreceptor ribbon synapses in the outer plexiform layer degenerate, and astroglia and microglia are strongly activated. Inner-retinal signal transmission is severely reduced. This fits the early cone-rod dysfunction seen in patients.

evidence.snippet: Histological results implied that ACBD5-deficient mice exhibit a moderate degeneration of photoreceptor, bipolar, ganglion and retinal pigment epithelial cells accompanied, however, by a prominent activation of astroglia and microglia.

evidence.snippet: Reduced a- and b-wave amplitudes from ffERG point to a severe functional dysregulation of retinal signal transduction with a focus at the level of the information-processing cell of the inner retina.

evidence.snippet: This series confirms retinal dystrophy and leukodystrophy as key features of ACBD5 deficiency with main symptoms of early onset visual decline, progressive spasticity, and cerebellar ataxia.

nodes.description: Unoxidized very-long-chain fatty acids, including C26:0, ultra-long species above C32 and very-long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, are built into phospholipids. In ACBD5-deficient mice the pattern is tissue-specific: ultra-long species rise in cerebellar phosphatidylcholines but not liver, and in the retina VLC-PUFA build up in the plexiform (synaptic) layers rather than in photoreceptor outer segments.

evidence.reference_title: Cerebellar and hepatic alterations in ACBD5-deficient mice are associated with unexpected, distinct alterations in cellular lipid homeostasis.
evidence.snippet: In line with the neurological pathology, unusual ultra-long chain fatty acids (C > 32) were elevated in phosphocholines from cerebelli but not liver indicating an organ-specific imbalance in fatty acid degradation and elongation pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Local accumulation of very long-chain PUFA in plexiform layers associates with retinal dysfunction in a mouse model of peroxisomal ACBD5-deficiency.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, VLC-PUFAs in ACBD5-deficient mice consistently accumulated in the inner retinal region from the outer (OPL) to inner plexiform layer (IPL).
